media:group.media:title: Blink-powered glasses monitor health
media:group.media:description:
In a new Northwestern University study, the team developed a wholly new type of smart glasses equipped with tiny sensors that harvest mechanical energy from facial movements and convert it into electrical power. Even a quick blink or an artery’s faint pulsing provides enough mechanical energy to activate the highly sensitive sensors.
Read the full story: https://news.northwestern.edu/stories/2026/10/blink-powered-glasses-could-keep-an-eye-on-health?fj=1 ____

media:group.media:title: Supramolecular polymers supercharge neuron growth
media:group.media:description:
Side-by-side videos showing the growth of mouse cortical neurons treated with positively charged supramolecular polymers (left) versus charge-segmented supramolecular polymers. Neurons on the right grew longer neurites — the long projections neurons use to communicate with other cells. They also formed more elaborate branches, gaining the ability to connect with neighboring cells.
Credit: Madison Strong (Stupp Laboratory), Center for Regenerative Nanomedicine, Northwestern University
Read more: https://news.northwestern.edu/stories/2026/10/researchers-unlock-new-level-of-precision-in-supramolecular-materials?fj=1 ____

entry.title: Just 20 minutes of calming music gives doctors a chance to recharge

media:group.media:title: Just 20 minutes of calming music gives doctors a chance to recharge
media:group.media:description:
While burnout in the medical field is well documented, affecting about half of healthcare workers, far fewer studies have explored ways to address it. Now, a Northwestern Medicine study has found one simple intervention may help.
Building on earlier Northwestern University research that found improvisatory music can lower blood pressure, slow breathing and induce a meditative brain state, Northwestern scientists tested whether the same approach could improve clinician wellbeing.
Read the full story: https://news.northwestern.edu/stories/2026/09/for-healthcare-workers-20-minutes-of-calming-music-offers-a-chance-to-recharge?fj=1#tab-panel1 ____

media:group.media:title: March through the Arch! 2026
media:group.media:description:
The tradition known as "March through the Arch" is a procession under the Northwestern's iconic entry gate, Arnold Weber Arch.
Each fall, incoming students, led by Northwestern University Marching Band, progress through campus to symbolically step onto the campus to begin their college experience. They are cheered on by current students, faculty and their families.
This year, new Northwestern President Mung Chiang joined the students in section 18, a symbolic nod to Chiang being Northwestern's 18th president. ____

entry.title: New drone nearly disappears in flight

media:group.media:title: New drone nearly disappears in flight
media:group.media:description:
Called the "Phantom Twist," new drone spins up to 25 times per second, which is too fast for the human eye to see it clearly. While it isn’t completely invisible, it morphs into a ghostly smudge that seamlessly blends into the background. The work eventually could lead to drones that monitor wildlife and survey the environment with less visual disruption.
Read more: https://news.northwestern.edu/stories/2026/07/new-spinning-drone-hides-in-plain-sight?fj=1

entry.title: Cell-inspired material captures energy and releases it on demand

media:group.media:title: Cell-inspired material captures energy and releases it on demand
media:group.media:description:
Watch a shape-shifting liquid transform into an energy-rich black gel that stores power for months.
Traditionally, harvesting energy, storing it and using it require separate materials or devices. The new platform merges all three functions into a single material, opening the door for adaptive, clean, renewable systems that don’t require plastics or metals.
Credit: Samuel I. Stupp/Northwestern University
